qs.hint: Ekjon manush nijer family te ki korechilo? Revival er bikkhato golpo ta dekho.
qs.why: Ben-Yehuda 'insisted on speaking only Hebrew to his family' = nijer ghore language choice. B te parents ghore language bondho kore, but oita ek jon specific person na.

qs.s: an explanation of why counting languages is affected by non-scientific factors
qs.ev: drawn on political rather than linguistic grounds
qs.hint: Language ar dialect er majhe line tana kivabe hoy? 'non-scientific' = politics type kichu.
qs.why: 'political rather than linguistic grounds' = non-scientific factor. 'more slogan than statistic' o tempting, but oita ekta figure er criticism, counting er karon na.

qs.s: an example of an organisation turning down a commercial offer
qs.ev: declined offers from large technology firms to purchase its Māori speech data
qs.hint: 'turning down' = refuse. Ke tech company der kache data bechte raji hoy nai?
qs.why: 'declined offers... to purchase' = turning down a commercial offer. E te o New Zealand ache, but okhane kono offer er kotha nai.

qs.s: an example of documents produced by outsiders being used to restore a language
qs.ev: using missionary records and early dictionaries
qs.hint: Kono living speaker chilo na, tobuo language fire esheche. Kader lekha record use kora hoyeche, sheta dekho.
qs.why: 'missionary records' = outsider der lekha documents, ar 'reintroduced it in homes' = restore. D te Hebrew er 'written tradition' o ache, kintu oita Hebrew speaker community r nijer lekha, outsider der na.

qs.s: the reason why moving to towns can weaken a language
qs.ev: typically marry outside their linguistic group
qs.hint: 'towns' = cities. Gram theke shohore gele language er upor ki effect, oi line ta khojo.
qs.why: 'Urban migration' = moving to towns, ar karon holo 'marry outside their linguistic group'. Stigma o B te ache, but oita moving er sathe related na.

qs.s: a mention of broadcasting being used to support a language
qs.ev: supported by a Welsh-language television channel launched in 1982
qs.hint: 'broadcasting' = TV ba radio. Wales er kotha je paragraph e ache dekho, F er broadcaster trap hote pare.
qs.why: 'television channel' = broadcasting ar 'supported' = support. F e ekta broadcaster ache, but setar kotha data na becha niye, language support kora niye na.

qs.q: According to paragraph B, parents in a community undergoing language shift stop using their traditional language mainly because
o: they themselves were punished for speaking it when they were at school.
they believe another language will give their children better opportunities.
their children refuse to learn it after moving to the cities for work.
it lacks the vocabulary needed for education, commerce and government.
qs.ev: hoping to improve their children's prospects
qs.hint: Parents er kotha je line e ache, oi line er majhe comma diye ekta reason ache. School er shasti ar city migration onno line er kotha.
qs.why: 'hoping to improve their children's prospects' = better opportunities er jonno. Punishment option e children der kotha bola hoyeche, parents keno chhare tar direct karon hisebe na.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention certain languages of South America?
o: To show that oral literature is especially easy to lose.
To illustrate grammar that may alter ideas about how people think.
To give an example of plant names unknown to Western science.
To argue that these languages are more complex than European ones.
qs.ev: grammatical structures that challenge assumptions about human cognition
qs.hint: 'for instance' er age ki bola hocche dekho, South America oi kothar example. Plant names Pacific er kotha.
qs.why: South America er language gula 'grammatical structures that challenge assumptions about human cognition' er example. Plant name option ta Pacific language er, ar complexity compare kora hoy nai.

qs.q: What point do scholars make about the revival of Hebrew?
o: It proves that any language can be revived if there is enough political will.
It succeeded mainly because of Ben-Yehuda's dictionary of modern words.
It offers limited guidance because the conditions behind it are rarely repeated.
It was achieved largely by giving formal lessons to adult immigrants.
qs.ev: Few endangered languages today enjoy any of these advantages
qs.hint: 'Scholars caution, however' theke porte thako. 'any language' type extreme option theke sabdhan.
qs.why: Circumstances 'exceptional' ar aj 'Few endangered languages' oi subidha pay = limited guidance. Political movement ekta factor, but 'any language can be revived' ulta conclusion.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude to the research from Canada?
o: It proves that reviving a language directly improves young people's health.
If confirmed, it suggests revivals may be worthwhile even with few speakers.
It contradicts the experience of the Miami Tribe in the American Midwest.
It supports the older view that success depends on producing native speakers.
qs.ev: If such findings hold, the value of a revival may lie as much in identity and well-being as in numbers
qs.hint: Sesh line er shuru 'If such findings hold' ekta hedge. 'proves' er moto strong word thakle sabdhan.
qs.why: 'If such findings hold' = if confirmed, ar 'as much in identity and well-being as in numbers' = speaker kom holeo value ache. 'proves' option beshi strong, writer 'tend to' ar 'If' diye hedge koreche.

summary.title: Immersion and technology
summary.text: Revival work in New Zealand began at a time when only a {1} of Māori people were fluent in their language. Pre-schools in which elderly community members looked after babies offered {2} exposure to the language, and the same approach was later extended to older pupils. In Wales, broadcasting and legal {3} have helped prevent any further fall in the number of speakers. Most experts conclude that {4} classes for grown-ups seldom result in fluency, and that what matters is passing the language on to small children. Technology, meanwhile, has made the recording of speakers much {5} than it was in the past, though the {6} of a few major languages on the internet may make smaller ones appear to have no place in modern life.

qs.ev: fewer than one in five Māori people could speak their language fluently
qs.hint: 'one in five' er cheyeo kom. Eta ki boro onsho naki choto onsho?
qs.why: 'fewer than one in five' = choto ongsho, tai minority. 'majority' grammar e boshe but number er sathe mele na.

qs.ev: immersed infants entirely in Māori
qs.hint: 'entirely' word ta dekho, er adjective synonym box e ache. Box e ulta meaning er word o ache, sabdhan.
qs.why: 'immersed... entirely' = puro exposure, kono English chhara. 'partial' mane ardhek, text er ulta.

qs.ev: legislation giving the language official status
qs.hint: Law ki diyeche Welsh ke? 'official status' er noun synonym khojo, 'funding' er kotha text e nai.
qs.why: 'official status' dewa = legal recognition. 'funding' boshe but law taka diyeche emon kotha nai.

qs.ev: formal lessons for adults rarely produce fluent speakers
qs.hint: 'grown-ups' = adults. Oi line e lessons er age kon adjective? 'informal' ulta trap.
qs.why: 'formal lessons' = class room style, structured classes. 'informal' meaning er ulta.

qs.ev: archived in hours rather than transcribed laboriously over months
qs.hint: 'hours rather than months' compare koro. Ekhon recording ager cheye ki hoyeche?
qs.why: 'in hours rather than... over months' = ekhon druto, mane faster. 'slower' ulta. Equipment 'inexpensive' sotti, but box e oi word nai.

qs.ev: the internet itself is overwhelmingly dominated by a few major languages
qs.hint: 'dominated by a few major languages' er noun form er moto word khojo. 'absence' ulta meaning.
qs.why: 'overwhelmingly dominated' = boro language gulo shob jaygay ache, mane prevalence. 'absence' boshe but meaning ulta.
